summary: Set 131 Session 1 of 3, 'The pin comes out, and the rule that replaces it'. Removed the 2026-08-05 verification-only outsourcing pin that Set 111 was named to lift and never did, and replaced it with a precedence-ordered Delegation Discipline in docs/ai-led-session-workflow.md: authority veto -> independence requirement -> risk gate -> context footprint -> model choice, in that order, with the order itself stated as the contract. Encoded the machine-readable half in router-config.yaml (outsourcing_mode: whenever-helpful, direct_work_reason_codes as a closed enum, an advisory child_budget, transport-keyed thresholds) and validated all four in config.py. Deleted the phantom delegation.direct_work_max_lines / direct_work_max_files knobs the doc had promised for twenty sets and that never existed. Replaced the '~50 lines of reasoned output' threshold, which measured emitted output, with a retained-input context-footprint trigger. Cross-provider verification then caught the defect that mattered: the new rule 2 claimed independence work must run on a different effective provider, but route() derived that exclusion only for session-verification, so the shipped code-review: sonnet pin handed an Anthropic orchestrator an Anthropic reviewer. Fixed by widening the derivation to the whole independence floor; round 3 then rejected that fix for over-widening the Set 123 S2 DIRECT_API degradation carve-out (an operator-authorized verification reduction scoped to session-verification alone) to code-review and security-review, which would have been the orchestrator self-authorizing a reduction. Re-scoped, and round 4 VERIFIED with both fixes accepted. TEST COMPOSITION (project-guidance requires this be stated, not presented as one clean run): pytest 4482 passed / 9 skipped in one invocation; mocha 1455 passing / 2 pending in one invocation; playwright 30 passed in the declared invocation plus vsix-first-run-walkthrough passing in a subsequent isolated run (57.6s, against the 300s budget it exhausted under load). Every test in all three suites executed and passed.

reason.specifics: Routed recommendation (s1-next-orchestrator-routed.md) said switch-due-to-cost to claude-sonnet-4.6. Not adopted, and the artifact is kept so the disagreement is auditable. Three reasons. (1) Its rationale is the naive substitution argument this set's own evidence corrected: at MATCHED input context the model-substitution lever is ~1.7-2x, not the 8.5x an uncontrolled per-model average suggests, and the dominant lever is transcript rotation at ~7-8x. (2) Spec trap T3: the orchestrator is the only actor holding write, shell and network rights, so downgrading the privileged seat to save money buys a confused-deputy path that the routed children's read-only sandbox does not close. The spec lists 'no orchestrator model change' as an explicit non-goal on exactly this reasoning. (3) The recommendation was produced BY claude-sonnet-4.6 recommending claude-sonnet-4.6; task_type=architecture is not in the independence floor, so no provider exclusion applied, which is correct behaviour but does make the advice self-interested. Session 2 is narrow, but narrowness is an argument about scope, not about who should hold the write bit.
